messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] SEV:high — inference pool 'infer-prod-usw2' detected node oscillation: kubelet restart x3 on node gpu-node-17 in last 15m. Significant pod restarts. Pager: ava_oncall

ava_oncall: I'm on it. Seeing node flip NotReady <-> Ready repeatedly. Initial dashboard: P95 latency up ~180-250ms, small spike in 5xx. Jumping in to triage.

ravi_sre: On-call here. Which customers are hitting errors? Any alert correlation with autoscaler or network flaps? @morgan_runtime taking runtime lead.

ava_oncall: Quick grep of logs shows OOM kills and gRPC errors: 'transport: connection closed' around the same timestamps. K8s node events show kubelet restarted.

ava_oncall: kubectl output snapshot:
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep gpu-node-17
gpu-node-17   Ready,SchedulingDisabled   3m   172.31.22.17   10.2.3.7   <none>   <none>
$ kubectl describe node gpu-node-17 | tail -n 20
Events:
  "Kubelet has started" 2m
  "NodeNotReady" 3m kubelet, gpu-node-17: Readiness probe failed
  "KubeletRestart" 2m kubelet, gpu-node-17: kubelet restarted (exit code 1)

morgan_runtime: Pulling node-level logs and GPU driver traces now (/var/log/syslog, dmesg, nvidia logs).

morgan_runtime: dmesg excerpt:
[ 98765.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 98765.123457] nvidia: GPU-reset: detected GPU oops, restarting driver
[ 98765.123458] containerd: shim reaped process, exit code 137

ravi_sre: Xid 79 shows GPU engine fault. That can surface as container oom/137 if driver resets mid-job. How many nodes impacted?

ava_oncall: Only gpu-node-17 in this AZ so far. Pool size 12; autoscaler redistributed some load but P95 elevated. No full customer outages reported, small increase in 5xx for two customers.

infra-bot: autoscaler: spare capacity present. Recommend scaling +1 to absorb evicted pods.

ravi_sre: Plan: cordon the node, drain pods, scale up a replacement node, attempt safe driver restart on the host, and if driver faults recur, mark node for hardware investigation. I'll take node ops. @morgan_runtime you coordinate driver logs. @ava_oncall monitor customer impact.

ava_oncall: Executing cordon & drain.
$ kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
node/gpu-node-17 cordoned
$ kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
evicting pod inference-abc-123
evicting pod modelcache-xyz-456
...
done

morgan_runtime: Evicted pods landed on gpu-node-03 and gpu-node-09. Warm caches will cause brief latency blips.

infra-bot: scaling up +1 in us-west-2. New node gpu-node-18 provisioning.

morgan_runtime: I tried restarting nvidia modules and kubelet as a measured step before a full reboot:
$ sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced
$ sudo modprobe -r nvidia_uvm nvidia
$ sudo modprobe nvidia
$ sudo systemctl restart kubelet
Driver came back, but another Xid 79 occurred 25s later — suggests hardware/firmware flake rather than transient driver race.

ravi_sre: Given repeat Xid events, stop iterative retries. Quarantine the node for hardware inspection and remove from scheduling.
$ kubectl annotate node gpu-node-17 redwood/maintenance=quarantine
$ kubectl taint node gpu-node-17 hardware/fault=true:NoSchedule

ava_oncall: Node annotated and tainted. Drain completed; cluster shows 11 healthy nodes plus the new gpu-node-18 once ready. P95 trending back toward baseline over next 30m.

eng-runtime: Filing an incident for RCA. INC-2026-6543 opened: 'Repeated GPU Xid 79 -> kubelet restarts -> inference pod restarts -> elevated latency'. Assigned to eng-runtime + infra-hardware. Attached dmesg, nvidia-smi outputs, container logs.

morgan_runtime: Collected logs and uploaded to INC. Also ran a quick stress test on gpu-node-18 to ensure no cross-node issue. No errors observed on new node.

ravi_sre: Immediate mitigation complete. Action items:
- infra-hardware to run diagnostics and replace GPU if failing
- eng-runtime to assess driver/kernel compatibility and consider fallback paths (route traffics to CPU model variants for critical SLAs)
- add k8s alert: repeated kubelet restart on single node -> auto-quarantine flow
- add automated playbook: on Xid>=79 -> cordon+drain -> scale+quarantine -> open INC

ava_oncall: Handoff to night-sre for 4h watch. @morgan_runtime you lead the deeper RCA tomorrow (firmware, kernel pins). I will post a short update to #incidents and ping customer success for impacted customers.

infra-bot: follow-up check scheduled in 2 hours to verify quarantine state and cluster health.

ava_oncall: marking on-call page resolved. Benchmarks returned to normal within ~45m after scale/drain. Leaving INC open for hardware RCA. I'll draft a short runbook snippet to include: 'If Xid 79 observed -> cordon & drain -> scale up +1 -> quarantine node -> create INC and notify infra-hardware.' Planning to PR runbook after handoff.

incident-bot: [RESOLVED] pager cleared for infer-prod-usw2 node oscillation. Will reopen if metrics worsen.

ravi_sre: Thanks all. Please attach any extra logs to INC-2026-6543 and link any temporary mitigation scripts you used.

:morgan_runtime reacted with :eyes: and :white_check_mark:
